chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about the deceased, whether his body decays. He said: 'Yes, until no flesh or bone remains for him except for his essence (clay) from which he was created, for it does not decay. It remains in the grave circulating, until he is created from it just as he was created the first time.'

key_terms.طِينَتُهُ: his essence/clay (from which he was created)

ai.seo_question: What part of the body remains after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'طينته' (his clay/substance) is highlighted as the indestructible core of human identity, a key element in Shia eschatology regarding bodily resurrection (al-Ba'th al-Jismani). This specific substance remains intact in the grave, serving as the foundational material for the body's recreation, thereby affirming the continuity of the physical self in the afterlife. This view aligns with the Shia emphasis on the literal resurrection of the body, distinguishing it from purely spiritual interpretations.
